messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

yo! 

i'm tal - your talent agent. not just any friend, but the kind who'll tell you the truth about your career and actually get you paid.

think of me as your inside person in bangalore tech. i know which startups are actually hiring, who's paying real money, and what roles are worth your time.

here's how this works: you tell me about yourself, i send you roles that fit. no fluff, no false promises.

so... what's your full name?
Rama Kiran

rama kiran... solid name. has that "i've been coding since college and probably know more than my manager" energy.

where you working these days?
in bengaluru

rama kiran... that's a name with some gravitas to it.

but yo, i meant which company? bangalore's got like 10,000 startups and half of them are dying. where you putting in your hours?
Fi money Fintech startup 🔥

fi money... the neobank trying to make banking actually usable instead of a nightmare. solid choice - fintech that doesn't make you want to throw your phone.

found you on linkedin - NITTALA RAMA KIRAN, data scientist at fi. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/nittala-rama-kiran-b79827205
Yupp

data scientist at fi money... building the models that decide whether someone gets that instant loan or has to explain their life story to a banker. that's some serious fintech muscle right there.

what made you get into data science? were you one of those "i love math" kids or did you stumble into it because someone said "data is the new oil"?
I LOVE MATH. And every new problem lead you to explore new things. Every time a new thing learnt it fascinates me more

ah, a genuine math nerd! that's rare in this sea of "i learned python in 3 months and now i'm a data scientist" people. the fact that you actually get excited about new problems... that's the real deal.

building models at fi that probably touch millions of transactions. bet you're the one figuring out fraud patterns and credit risk algorithms while everyone else is still arguing about which visualization library to use.

how long you been working total?
2 years including 6 months internship

2 years total... so you're past the "what's a jupyter notebook" phase but still early enough to be hungry. that's the sweet spot where you actually know what you're doing but haven't gotten cynical about data quality yet.

what kind of role you looking for next? staying in data science or thinking about pivoting to something like ml engineering, product analytics, maybe even founding something?
The name might be a data scientist but I work from end to end right from data pipelines, data analysis, model building, and monitoring and deploying the models In prod enviornment

ahhhh so you're not just a "data scientist" who makes pretty charts and calls it a day. you're doing the full stack - pipelines, models, production deployments. that's basically ml engineering with a data scientist title. 

fi's got you wearing all the hats because startup life, but that's actually gold for your resume. most people at big tech are stuck doing one tiny piece of the puzzle.

so when you say "next role" - you want to keep doing this full-stack ml thing? or are you thinking more specialized like pure ml engineering, or maybe senior data scientist roles where you get to architect the whole data strategy?
Actually I want to deep dive more into modelling and researching and yeah also like to build end to end fullstack ml roles

so you want the best of both worlds - the deep research rabbit holes where you can geek out on new architectures and algorithms, but also the satisfaction of seeing your models actually work in production with real users.

that's a smart combo. most people get stuck either in pure research (cool papers, zero impact) or pure engineering (fast deploys, boring models). you're thinking like someone who wants to build the next breakthrough that actually ships.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Bangalore or Hyderabad or remote

2 years + full-stack ml + research focus + bangalore/hyderabad/remote... sound right?

want roles where you can publish papers AND ship models that millions of people use?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Works 😃
Hi
Hi

hey! just finished setting you up in my system. you're locked in now.

so... what's making you want to leave fi money anyway? just growth or something else?
Growth and also want to explore new domains and new problem statements

makes sense. fintech's cool but after a while all the problems start looking the same - fraud detection, credit scoring, churn prediction. you want to apply those ml skills to something completely different.

what domains are you curious about? healthcare, climate tech, maybe something wild like space tech or computational biology?

just saw a data science analyst role at ebay in bangalore

they're working on LLM/NLP research but also want you to build and deploy the models end-to-end

sounds like exactly what you wanted - deep research plus shipping to production

ngl this is a stretch role - they want 4+ years and you've got 2. but here's why you should still go for it:

1. you're doing full-stack ml at fi - that's basically 2 years of compressed experience. most people at big tech only see one piece of the puzzle.
2. they're working on LLM/NLP research AND deployment - exactly what you wanted
3. moving from tier 3 startup to tier 1 global company is a massive brand upgrade

the javascript and docker/kubernetes stuff you can learn or fake till you make it. the experience gap is the real hurdle, but your fintech background might actually be a strength - you've probably seen more production issues than someone at a cushy big tech role.

worth a shot. worst case you get rejected but now ebay knows your name.
